newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila editor killed, drugs ring suspected.
newsitem.headline: Manila editor killed, drugs ring suspected.

text.p: A journalist who specialised in exposing drug syndicates and police corruption was shot dead in a taxi on Tuesday as he struggled with his assassin, police said.
Danny Hernandez, the news editor of a popular tabloid daily, was shot in the back of the neck as he grappled with his killer, who police said was probably a professional hitman.

Hernandez had been receiving death threats from what he suspected were members of drugs rings, according to colleagues at the widely circulated People's Journal Tonight, where he wrote a feisty column called "Sunday Punch".
"I condemn this killing of a crusading and hard-hitting media man," President Fidel Ramos said in a statement.
He ordered a joint probe by the National Bureau of Investigation and the police "to identify, arrest and bring to the bar of justice the perpetrators".
Hernandez's death early Tuesday morning was the latest in a string of murders of Philippine journalists.
Hours after the killing, an anonymous caller phoned the Journal saying his group was responsible for the death. Another caller said more killings would follow, a Journal staffer said.

"The slaying of Hernandez is a major blow to press freedom but its chilling effect won't deter the country's journalists from... exposing crime and other irregularities," the National Press Club (NPC) said in a statement. Hernandez became the 32nd journalist to die violently since democracy was restored in the country in 1986 with the ousting of the late president Ferdinand Marcos in a popular revolt.
Last December, a veteran broadcasting editor, also known for exposing criminal activities, was shot dead near Manila. Two people are facing trial for the killing.
Since Marcos's overthrow, the Philippine press has become one of the most open in Asia, its front pages plastered with headlines about corruption and organised crime.
Police said Hernandez left the Journal office just before dawn and took a cab he did not know had been stolen hours earlier. The cab was apparently waiting for him, police said.
"The gunman might have gotten in later," an investigator said. "He fired twice, missing his first shot because Hernandez apparently struggled... then he hit him in the nape."
Police said Hernandez had been carrying a pistol but apparently was not able to shoot back.
Colleagues said Hernandez had told them he had been practising shooting because of the death threats and quoted him as saying, "It's bettter to have a chance to fight back."
In his last column which appeared on the morning he died, Hernandez wrote of alleged payoffs to police by crime syndicates.
"I am convinced the murderers are related to drug pushers," said governor Roberto Pagdanganan of Bulacan province. Hernandez often wrote about drugs traffickers in Bulacan.
